children: The offshore yuan edged higher to around 6.70 per dollar on Thursday, after holding steady in the previous session, as China broadens currency clearing in a bid to advance the yuan’s internationalization.

The Shanghai Clearing House started central counterparty (CCP) services for spot trades in the Singapore dollar, New Zealand dollar and Thai baht on Sept. 14, with twelve banks clearing 996 million yuan ($148 million) in the first session.

The move could set the stage for more currencies to be cleared directly against the yuan as Beijing seeks to broaden its global use, alongside efforts by Chinese banks this year to expand clients’ access to direct yuan trading amid growing cross-border trade and investment.

Meanwhile, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is set to meet Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng this weekend for final preparatory talks ahead of the Sept. 24 summit between Presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping in the US.

title: Offshore Yuan Edges Higher
